answer: A concrete defense is escalating proof-of-work per action: before any rewarded action, each identity must solve a fresh verifiable-delay puzzle, and difficulty rises with how fast that identity acts. Honest work barely notices the cost, but a farmer running a thousand clones pays compute and wall-clock time for every fake action, so the marginal clone earns less than it burns. Think of the network as a graph where each vertex is an identity: a raven that copies itself still has to fly the same puzzle each time, and a lotus that blooms once cannot be photocopied into a field for free.
